# Module 2: Sales and follow-up

*Every enquiry answered and every quote followed up, without retyping it all.*

**Who does it in a small business:** Owner or sales rep, office admin.

## The typical process

Every business does it a bit differently. This is the common shape we see.

| # | Step | What happens | Tools | Where time goes |
|:-:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Enquiry lands | Phone, email, website form | Gmail, Outlook, Website form, Phone |  |
| 2 | Sort the inbox | Work out which emails are real enquiries | Outlook, Gmail | slow |
| 3 | Qualify it | Budget, timing, who decides | Phone |  |
| 4 | Write it up | Call notes typed or dictated into the CRM | HubSpot, Excel, Voice note | copy-paste |
| 5 | Quote and follow up | Send the quote, chase it, answer questions | Outlook, Phone | slow |
| 6 | Won: hand over | Fill in the handover form for the office or crew | Word, Outlook, HubSpot | copy-paste |

## Where the time goes

From businesses APG has audited, anonymised. Hours are staff estimates, not measurements.

- Sorting the inbox: 1.5 to 2 h a day per salesperson
- Copying emails into the CRM: 20 to 40 min a day per person
- Follow-up emails written the next morning, called the most time-consuming part of the job
- A 20-question handover typed from the CRM into an email

## Step 1: the intake

`/sales-intake`: Map how an enquiry becomes a won job: who answers, where notes go, and when you follow up.

It hands back your own version of the map above, with your tools and your hours, then suggests which skill to build first.

## The skills

- **Inbox sorter** (connected): Flags the real enquiries and drafts the first reply
- **Call note to CRM** (connected): Speak after the call: note, task and follow-up email drafted
- **Handover pack** (connected): The won job's handover questions filled from the quote and emails
